definition: Gabriella Sanniti di Baja (born 29 January 1950) is a retired Italian computer scientist specializing in pattern recognition, including digital geometry and skeletonization.
details: Gabriella Sanniti di Baja (born 29 January 1950) is a retired Italian computer scientist specializing in pattern recognition, including digital geometry and skeletonization.

explainer.lead: Gabriella Sanniti di Baja is an Italian computer scientist in pattern recognition, known for skeletonization and distance transforms, and the first woman to lead the International Association for Pattern Recognition (IAPR).
explainer.knownFor: Skeleton and distance-transform methods for describing digital shapes, and three decades of leadership in the IAPR.

contributions.name: Skeletonization
contributions.detail: Algorithms that reduce a shape to a thin, stable “skeleton” that can be turned back into the original—used for shape analysis and recognition.

contributions.name: Distance transforms
contributions.detail: Efficient digital approximations of Euclidean distance, such as the (3,4) weighted distance, that power skeleton extraction.

contributions.name: Leading the IAPR
contributions.detail: IAPR Secretary for three terms (1994–2000), then its first woman President (2000–2002); general chair of ICPR 2008 and 2016.

contributions.name: Editorial work
contributions.detail: Former editor-in-chief of the journal Pattern Recognition Letters.

timeline.what: Doctorate, University of Naples Federico II
Publishes reversible skeletons from the (3,4) distance transform; becomes IAPR Secretary
Becomes the first woman President of the IAPR
Retires as CNR director of research

keyWorks.title: Well-Shaped, Stable, and Reversible Skeletons from the (3,4)-Distance Transform
